_doc: The manifest that drives the user guide (tools/guide/build-guide.mjs) and the keyboard reference of the Accessibility page (tools/copy/build-trust-pages.mjs). It describes the CURRENT behaviour of the Tranche 0 build named in `release`, as established by the Help dialog text that the patches of tools/t0/patches put into that build, the app's own key handler after the same patches, the release notes and the committed tests. It never describes planned behaviour: anything that is not in the live baseline (the site as served on 2026-09-30) carries a `since` train and is printed as a since-version note. `tools/guide/check-parity.mjs` compares this file with the patched Help text, the patched key handler and the patched site menu and reports every mismatch. Wording (`label`, `text`) follows docs/content/STYLEGUIDE.md; `help` holds the exact row the Help dialog shows in this release (it may break the style guide: that is reported, not hidden).

hotkeys.label: Play or pause
hotkeys.text: Starts or stops the playback. With a button focused, Space presses that button instead.

hotkeys.label: Next moment
hotkeys.text: Moves forward by one moment.

hotkeys.label: Previous moment
hotkeys.text: Moves back by one moment.

hotkeys.label: Forward 12 moments
hotkeys.text: Moves forward by 12 moments. The Help panel calls this one hour; the time between moments varies, so it is not one hour of battle time everywhere (see About the clock).

hotkeys.label: Back 12 moments
hotkeys.text: Moves back by 12 moments (the Help panel calls this one hour).

hotkeys.label: Jump to July 1
hotkeys.text: Jumps to the first moment of July 1 (dawn) and pauses.

hotkeys.label: Jump to July 2
hotkeys.text: Jumps to the first moment of July 2 and loads that day's positions.

since_note.R1c: The day's positions are loaded before the jump lands. On earlier builds the map can show empty or stale positions after a day jump.

hotkeys.label: Jump to July 3
hotkeys.text: Jumps to the first moment of July 3 and loads that day's positions.

since_note.R1c: The day's positions are loaded before the jump lands.

hotkeys.label: Slower
hotkeys.text: Halves the playback speed, down to 0.25 times.
evidence: tools/guide/lib/t0src.mjs extractKeyHandler (speed floor read from the handler)

hotkeys.label: Faster
hotkeys.text: Doubles the playback speed, up to 16 times.
evidence: tools/guide/lib/t0src.mjs extractKeyHandler (speed ceiling read from the handler)

hotkeys.label: Normal speed
hotkeys.text: Returns the playback speed to 1 times. The speed label reads 1x (base speed).

since_note.R1c: The label no longer describes a clock rate: the playback is a time-lapse.

hotkeys.label: Zoom
hotkeys.text: Scroll the wheel over the map to zoom in or out.

hotkeys.label: Pan
hotkeys.text: Press and drag on the map to move it. A press on the map hands keyboard focus back to the page, so the time keys keep working afterwards.

since_note.R1a: A click, a drag or a unit selection no longer leaves keyboard focus on the map, so the arrow keys step through time as this guide says.

hotkeys.label: Move the map from the keyboard
hotkeys.text: Press Tab until the map has focus. The arrow keys then pan the map instead of stepping through time, plus and minus zoom it, and Shift with the arrow keys rotates and tilts it. Esc hands the keys back to the page.

help.desc: Arrow keys then pan it instead of stepping the clock, + / - zoom it, Shift + arrows rotate and tilt it; Esc gives the keys back

hotkeys.label: Select a unit
hotkeys.text: Click a unit to select it and pin its details. From Search, a unit can also be chosen with the keyboard.

since_note.R1b: A unit can be selected from Search by keyboard: type in the field, press Down arrow to move into the list and Enter to choose a unit; focus then moves to the unit's details.

hotkeys.label: Close or deselect
hotkeys.text: Closes the open panel or card and clears the selected unit. With several things open, Esc closes the topmost one first: the event card, then the story card, then the guided tour.

since_note.R1a: Esc also clears the pinned unit and closes Map Layers and the Distance tool; it closes the story card, event card and tour one at a time.

hotkeys.label: Filter panel
hotkeys.text: Opens or closes the filter panel.

hotkeys.label: Unit search
hotkeys.text: Opens or closes the unit search panel.

hotkeys.label: Bookmarks
hotkeys.text: Opens or closes the bookmarks panel.

hotkeys.label: Legend
hotkeys.text: Shows or hides the legend.

hotkeys.label: Minimap
hotkeys.text: Shows or hides the minimap.

hotkeys.label: Help
hotkeys.text: Shows or hides the Help panel. It lists these keys.

hotkeys.label: Heatmap
hotkeys.text: The heatmap key was removed in release R1a. Nothing in the map read it.

gestures.label: Pan
gestures.text: Drag one finger on the map to move it.

gestures.label: Zoom
gestures.text: Pinch with two fingers to zoom in or out.

gestures.label: Select a unit
gestures.text: Tap a unit to see its details.

gestures.label: Play or pause
gestures.text: The play button starts or stops the playback.

gestures.label: Step
gestures.text: The two arrow buttons step back or forward by one moment.

gestures.label: Timeline
gestures.text: Drag the bar to move through July 1 to 3.

help.desc: Drag the bar to move through July 1–3

gestures.label: Speed
gestures.text: The speed button changes the playback speed.

gestures.label: Jump to a day
gestures.text: The three day buttons jump to the start of July 1, 2 or 3.

help.desc: Jump to the start of a day

gestures.label: Tools
gestures.text: The Tools button opens a sheet with search, filter, roster, legend, bookmarks and the extra pages.

help.desc: Search, filter, roster, legend, bookmarks and more

toolbar.note: Tooltips of the desktop toolbar buttons in the baseline bundle, in order. This guide documents the ones whose behaviour the Help text, the release notes or a committed test establish; the others are named and not described.

documented.Help: Opens the Help panel (key ?). Since R1b it is a dialog that keeps Tab inside it and closes with Esc.
documented.Soldier's Eye View (Street View): Opens a list of eight viewpoints. Each opens in Google Street View in Google Maps (since R1c the label says so).
documented.Follow Your Ancestor: Opens a panel for following one regiment through the battle. Since R1c it loads all three days before it draws.

tools.text: Find a regiment, battery, story or battlefield location by name.
Show the unit positions at two different moments, side by side.
Director Mode moves the camera to where the most units are engaged. Follow Cam stays with one regiment.

Pick a vantage point and see how high it stands. The page ranks the height of 30 places on the field. It is not a line-of-sight map: trees, buildings, fences and gun smoke often decided what a soldier could see.
Move units and change their status at a chosen moment to explore a hypothetical. It is not history. Nothing is saved, and reloading the page resets it.
Ask about a regiment, a commander, a place or a moment. Answers come only from this site's own records. It is a search of those records, not an AI.
Read all 24 stories in order, each with its full text and a link to its place on the map.
Nine decisions where the battle might have gone differently, as historians have argued them.
A short guide to the battle for students and classrooms, by day.
What happened to the two armies, the town and the ground after July 3. It is an overview drawn from published histories, not built from unit-by-unit records.
Pick a regiment or battery and follow its three days as one story: commander, casualties and recorded positions.
Search regiments by state or by a commander's surname. The site lists regiments, not individual soldiers; to find a soldier by name use the National Park Service's Soldiers and Sailors System.
Corps-by-corps strength across the three days. The curves are modelled from each corps' recorded engagement periods: they show when losses concentrated, not observed strength at each moment.
Make a one-page reference sheet for a regiment, to print or save as a PDF from the browser's print dialog.
Plays a sound made in your browser that follows how many units are engaged at each moment. You turn the sound on yourself.
A running total of casualties across the three days, built from the same data as the Casualty Dashboard.
Accumulates the recorded unit positions into one map, so places where units were positioned often stand out.

Build a guided tour with your own stops and notes and share it as a file. Live Sync connects two browsers through a public connection service and can be unavailable; exporting and importing a tour always works.
Record a video of the camera flying across a stretch of the battle. It is made in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

tools_hidden.text: Needs a phone with a camera, GPS and compass. It is in beta and is not listed in the menu in this release; the page is still reachable by its address.
tools_hidden.since_note: Removed from the menu in R1a (tools/t0/patches/PG-core.json PGC-nav-hide-ar).

deeplinks.note: Read by the app when it loads. The parameters {tick}, {day}, {unit}, {vignette}, {ancestor}, {z} and {ll} arrived in release R1c; {layout} arrived in release R1b. Every value is validated; anything invalid is ignored and the map opens at its defaults.

params.name: tick
params.text: A moment number from 1 to 675. Wins over {day}.

params.name: day
params.text: 1, 2 or 3: the first moment of that day (moments 1, 226 and 451). Used only when no valid {tick} is given.

params.name: unit
params.text: A unit id. The unit is selected and its details pinned.

params.name: vignette
params.text: A story id. The map moves to that story's moment. Used only when no valid {tick} or {day} is given.

params.name: ancestor
params.text: A regiment id. Opens the panel for following one regiment.

params.name: z
params.text: Map zoom. Values are kept between 11 and 18.

params.name: ll
params.text: Map centre as latitude,longitude, or the two parameters lat and lng. Accepted only inside the battlefield (latitude 39.7 to 39.93, longitude -77.38 to -77.1).

params.name: layout
params.text: mobile or desktop: forces that layout instead of the automatic choice (phones and touch tablets up to 834 px wide, and landscape phones, get the phone layout).

examples.text: Opens at the start of July 2.
Opens at moment 538 with the 1st Minnesota Volunteer Infantry selected.
Opens at the moment of the story The Cannonade.

known_differences.text: The Help panel and some pages still say tick and five minutes, and call 12 moments one hour. Moments are not five minutes apart everywhere; read the moment as a place in the story, not a fixed length of time.
evidence: tools/guide/check-parity.mjs (Help text against the style guide)

known_differences.text: Clock labels can be hours off in places. Release R1c changes only the date (July 1, 2 and 3 instead of dates up to July 9); the clock itself is waiting on a decision about the time model.

The Monuments button is in the toolbar, but it shows nothing in this release. The star layer that appeared when it was pressed was removed from the site in production, and restoring it properly is on the owner's list.
The heatmap key and the in-map sound switch were removed in release R1a. Immersive Mode is the page that plays sound.

Some labels on screen use older names, for example the menu is called Extra Features and one page is called Battle Reports. This guide uses the names the style guide settles on and gives the on-screen label beside the first mention.
Ask the Historian searches this site's records. The count shown on its page is computed from the loaded files.

Everything in this guide was checked against the release's text, key handler and tests. Release R1c has been run only in Chrome on a desktop computer (touch was emulated). Safari, Firefox, Samsung Internet and real phones have not been tested.
